reify-audit's jcodemunch seam fails soft at TWO independent layers, and a test that covers only the first still admits a vacuous pass. Layer 1 (construction): `src/bin/reify-audit.rs:797` prints `reify-audit: jcodemunch unreachable at '<url>': …` when `JcodemunchClient::initialize` fails and degrades to `NoopJCodemunchOps`. Layer 2 (per call): each `RealJCodemunchOps` method matches on `call_tool(...)` and on `Err` prints its own breadcrumb and returns `Vec::new()` — `src/jcodemunch_client.rs:1074` `jcodemunch get_changed_symbols:`, `:1117` `jcodemunch find_references(<name>):`, `:1135` `jcodemunch get_dead_code_v2:`, `:1152` `jcodemunch get_untested_symbols:`, `:1168` `jcodemunch get_layer_violations:`. Layer 2 fires AFTER a successful handshake, so the layer-1 breadcrumb is silent, the §4.3 freshness gate has already admitted, the binary exits 0, and it serializes a well-formed EMPTY findings array. `count_symbols(index_dir, repo_id) > 0` does not discriminate — it reads the index DB directly and says nothing about whether the serve answered the tools/call.</content>

EscalationQueue.make_id(task_id) is an ID MINTER, not a dedup guard: it increments and persists a durable per-task counter (queue_dir/esc-{task_id}.seq) and returns a strictly-increasing id on every call, so two calls for the same task_id yield esc-N and esc-N+1. Code that files an escalation from a repeating condition (a retry loop, a per-resolution callback, a periodic sweep) and relies on make_id for "one record per task" will silently file one record per occurrence and bury the operator. The established in-repo dedup idiom is instead get_by_task(task_id, status='pending') filtered on the filer's own agent_role — see the sentinel escalations in orchestrator/harness.py (comment at ~:6390 "Deduped to one open at a time (via get_by_task + agent_role filter)") and Harness._escalate_cascade_status_rejection. A distinct variant exists for born-at-L2 records: find_pending_l2_by_root_cause(<fixed literal>), used by _file_structural_exhaustion_l2.</content>

Reify has NO `f(geometry) -> scalar/bool` stdlib function anywhere: `volume`, `surface_area`, `is_watertight` etc. are absent from the compiler's name registry. The blocker is structural — `reify_types::Value` has no geometry variant, so geometry exists only as `GeomRef` in the IR and `GeometryHandleId` as a per-build local inside `Engine::build_geometry`; handles are never stored in a value cell, so a plain stdlib call evaluated through reify-expr has no way to see one. Any geometry-query function must therefore capture its argument by NAME at compile time (via a dedicated `CompiledExprKind` variant), not as an evaluated `Value` argument.</content>

Implementer pre-flight gotcha (task 4647): a plan step that says "NEW FILE <path>" may describe a file a PREREQUISITE step already created and committed. The startup protocol's pre-flight only checks `git status`/`git diff HEAD` for UNCOMMITTED work, so a clean tree gives no warning, and using the Write tool then silently clobbers the committed scaffolding (here, ~560 lines of B1-B6 scenario builders from pre-1 were replaced by a from-scratch rewrite). Before Write-ing any file a step calls NEW, run `git log --oneline --all -- <path>` or `test -e <path>`; if it exists, APPEND to it instead. Recovery is cheap if caught before the commit is built on: `git checkout <prior-sha> -- <path>`, re-apply the additions, then `git commit --amend`, and verify the result is purely additive with `git diff <prior-sha> -- <path> | grep '^-[^-]'` returning nothing.</content>

CORRECTION to canonical PTODO entry 35e0187a (topic `ptodo-phantom-tracking-phrases`), case (3). That entry warns "A cite you added later goes terminal (done/cancelled) -> it becomes an `orphaned` High-severity finding." For the phantom-tracking lane on a NON-MARKER prose line that is FALSE, and the fear it creates is the very thing the 2026-08-20 curator correction was trying to remove.

Read from source at crates/reify-audit/src/ptodo.rs (verified 2026-08-27 on task 6810): scan_file computes `let has_canon = has_canonical_cite(line)` per PHYSICAL LINE (~line 897), and arm (6) is `} else if phantom_phrase(line) && !has_canon {` (~line 993) with NO else branch. So once you add a same-line `#NNNN`, arm (6) is skipped and NOTHING is pushed — provided no earlier arm matches, which for a plain prose comment is exactly the case: arm (3) needs `\b(TODO|FIXME|HACK)\b\s*[(:]` (find_comment_marker, ptodo.rs:52-59) and arms (4) stub-macro / (5) allow(dead_code) are .rs-ONLY. No LineClass::Cited is emitted, so the cite never reaches the beta liveness lane and can NEVER become orphaned/unknown-id. This agrees with entry 9b3fe0a9 ("a bare #NNNN cite in ordinary prose is NOT a marker and is therefore never scanned") and generalises it to the phantom-tracking arm specifically.

PRACTICAL UPSHOT: citing a real live task on a phantom-phrase prose line is a strictly safe, terminal fix — no orphaning risk to weigh. Case (3) of 35e0187a only applies when the line ALSO carries a real TODO/FIXME/HACK marker or (.rs only) a stub macro / allow(dead_code) deferral, which routes the cite into the liveness lane. The flip side is that the discharged claim is never re-checked: when the cited task completes, the "tracked separately as #NNNN" sentence silently goes stale. Filed as a low-priority follow-up from task 6810 (escalation id agent-followup-6810, ticket tkt_0RSY04VQQ9JESXRC7ZFKSY628J) to decide whether arm (6) should gain an else pushing LineClass::Cited, or whether section 8.3 should record this as a second deliberate divergence.

PLACEMENT GOTCHA worth keeping: because has_canon is per-line with no above-line lookback for arm (6), a wrapped comment sentence can strand the phrase on a continuation line away from its cite. Task 6810's fixture had `// OWNED BY #6653 (...)` on line 15 and the bare fragment `// tolerance hides is tracked separately.` on line 17 — the #6653 two lines up did not protect it. Fix by pulling the whole sentence onto ONE line that carries the cite, so a future re-wrap cannot re-open the regression.</content>

CONVENTION (dark-factory, esc-4696-3, commit 433c8f0fea): WIDENING A DETECTION GATE MUST NOT WIDEN A DESTRUCTIVE REPAIR. Task 4696 widened five markup gates from the param-blind detect() to the schema-aware detect_for(), which was correct. But shared.toolcall_markup.repair() accepts an EMPTY tail — a candidate closing tag sitting at end-of-string parses to {} and still returns clean_value = value[:candidate.start()]. Composing the two turned any prose that legitimately ENDS by quoting a tag pair into a silent TRUNCATION reported as outcome 'repaired' with recovered_names empty: text destroyed, nothing recovered, nothing surfaced for adjudication. It reproduced on BOTH widened consumers — plan_tools (persisted atomically by _read_plan_repaired) and scripts/sweep_toolcall_markup.py, whose widening is by every sibling KEY of the containing object under an --apply lane touching ~1124 dead meta-roots.

THE GENERAL RULE: when a gate is widened by NAME, the repairer behind it must be re-checked for any accept path that requires no EVIDENCE. Here the discriminator is that an empty tail means there was no absorbed argument, so the 'repair' is pure text loss. The fix refuses a candidate whose tail is empty, whose name != param, and whose closer is not one of the fixed ENVELOPE_LITERALS — leaving the value byte-identical and routing it to the human queue ('unrepairable' / 'refused' + quoted_only residue) instead of rewriting it.

THREE SUB-CONVENTIONS worth reusing:
1. Fix at the SHARED CHOKEPOINT, not at each call site. Both consumers inherited the fix and neither grew a second policy layer (INV-5). The rejected alternative — narrowing the gates back to the field's own name — also closes the loss but BLINDS detection to a real cross-field leak. Prefer 'keep it SEEN, decline to guess' over 'stop looking'.
2. A refusal that leaves data byte-identical and visible beats a repair that is right most of the time. plan_tools already had the right shape (an all-refusals branch that declines the write-back); the sweep already had the right discriminator (has_leak_signature) but consulted it only on the refusal path.
3. WHEN WRITING A NEGATIVE CONTROL for these markup guards, check the specimen tag name is one the WIDENING contributed, not a member of the fixed ENVELOPE_LITERALS (description/parameter/details/content). My first draft used 'description', which is exempt by design, and the test failed for that reason rather than pinning anything. Use a name like 'priority'/'decision'/'summary'.</content>
